_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4b, IC4-R1). `pairs` is the plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides. The confused pairings (Ney/Lannes, Massena/Davout) drawn twice each.

who.Ney: Ney — a bold marshal, famous for his courage and his impatience to fight.
who.Davout: Davout — a careful marshal, strict, exact, who counts every man and never wastes one.
who.Murat: Murat — a bold cavalry marshal who loves to ride and charge.
who.Lannes: Lannes — a bold marshal who marches to the sound of the guns and leads assaults himself.
who.Massena: Masséna — a stubborn marshal who never gives up ground he holds.
who.Bernadotte: Bernadotte — a slow, politic marshal who is never in a hurry and always has an excuse.

pairs.line1: Leave it to me, Sire. I'm moving now, and quickly.
pairs.line2: As I see fit, Sire. Wherever the guns are loudest, that's where you'll find me.

pairs.line1: We got the worst of it, Sire. I'll look harder before the next assault.
pairs.line2: I took a beating, Sire. I'll go slower, but I can't bear it long.

pairs.line1: I'd keep this ground, Sire. It's mine now, and worth keeping.
pairs.line2: Let me hold here, Sire, with every company counted and in place.

pairs.line1: Today is yours, Sire. My task is written down, every man and every order counted, for tomorrow.
pairs.line2: Your order first, Sire. My task will keep, and so will my ground.

pairs.line1: No change. Every post is manned and every count is right.
pairs.line2: Quiet for the moment. I'm listening for the guns.

pairs.line1: On his heels, Sire. He can hear us coming.
pairs.line2: The corps is moving up, Sire, at a comfortable pace.

pairs.line1: No one to chase today. A pity.
pairs.line2: Nothing to report. I give up nothing.

pairs.line1: Bolder still? Give me the squadrons and a loose rein.
pairs.line2: Boldly, Sire — very well. But nothing will be wasted.

pairs.line1: Boldly it is. Now I won't have to hold myself back.
pairs.line2: Boldly, Sire? Then the squadrons ride at full gallop.

pairs.line1: You recalled me once before I'd begun, Sire. I've kept that in mind.
pairs.line2: You overruled me once, Sire. I've not forgotten — but I'll go now.

pairs.line1: I regret it, Sire. The conditions were poor.
pairs.line2: It went wrong, Sire. I held my ground as long as I could.

pairs.line1: Done, Sire. I trust you'll find it was handled sensibly.
pairs.line2: Done, Sire, and no fuss about it. Where are the guns next?

rows.line: Bored of this, Sire. The horses and I have changed it.
I'll not do the same thing a third day, Sire. A fixed habit wastes men.
I've changed it, Sire. I'll stay on what is mine, but not like that.
Sitting through the same again would drive me mad. I've changed it.
I've made a small change, Sire. Nothing risky, I assure you.
Two days of that was plenty, Sire. I've changed it, and my ear is on the guns.
You pulled me away from the guns once, Sire. Don't do it twice.
You gave another man the task that was mine, Sire. I remember.
I was passed over once. I'd rather you checked the rolls to see who is senior.
You overruled me once, Sire. I've not forgotten — but I'll go now.
I was recalled once in the middle of a chase. I've not forgotten it.
Last time I was called back. I'd like to finish this one.
Done! Tell the others how a horseman manages it.
Done, Sire, and done in order. Not a man wasted.
Done, Sire, and no fuss about it. Where are the guns next?
The task is finished, Sire. Not an inch of it given back.
Done, Sire. I trust you'll find it was handled sensibly.
Finished, Sire. Find me another fight now.
As I see fit, Sire? What I hold is mine, and I take what lies next to it.
My own judgement, Sire? Then I march to the guns.
Very well, Sire. Not a man spent that I can't account for.
Free rein, Sire? The squadrons are saddled already.
Very good, Sire. I'll move when the moment is right, and not before.
No task, Sire? I'll find a fight myself now, before I go mad sitting here.
A win, Sire, and I want the next fight now.
A victory, Sire. What we won stays mine, and I'll risk a little more.
We won, Sire. I may venture a little more.
A victory. I'll accept slightly worse odds now, once the rolls are counted.
Another win, Sire. The horses and I will ride farther now.
A good day. The columns have their blood up, Sire.
